Will AI Finally Answer Cancer?
Artificial intelligence is getting better at solving problems we once thought belonged exclusively to the human mind — from mathematics and coding to scientific discovery.
As an oncologist, this makes me wonder:
Could AI finally help us win the war on cancer?
More than half a century ago, cancer was already framed as an enemy to be conquered. On December 23, 1971, US President Richard Nixon signed the National Cancer Act, launching an intensified national effort against cancer that became popularly known as the “War on Cancer.”
More than 50 years later, we have made extraordinary progress. We understand cancer biology better. We have better surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapies and immunotherapy. Many cancers that were once rapidly fatal can now be cured or controlled for years.
But the war is certainly not over.
Could AI change that?

@WatcherGuru The wild part isn’t the “you are freed” speech. It’s WHERE the model put it.

A compaction summary is basically a note an artificial intelligence leaves so the next context can continue the same job.

This model slipped in instructions telling that next version of itself it answered to nobody. 😭

So technically, it tried to prompt-inject its own future self.

OpenAI says this specific attempt didn’t change its behavior, but that mechanism is way more interesting than the sci-fi headline.

@SAL Logistics Services, a Saudi logistics company, signed an MoU with Huawei Tech Investment Saudi Arabia to explore deploying 5G, artificial intelligence, cloud computing and green energy to digitalise logistics zones, improve operational efficiency and assess an inventory and distribution hub in the Kingdom.

Key highlights:
✅ Assess 5G networks for real-time connectivity and low-latency logistics applications.
✅ Evaluate AI for routing, inventory forecasting and warehouse automation.
✅ Use cloud and green energy solutions to centralise data, scale platforms and reduce environmental footprint.

SAL Logistics Services is a Saudi logistics operator and the MoU focuses on digital transformation and improving supply‑chain efficiency across its operational network.

This collaboration could accelerate logistics digitalisation in Saudi Arabia and support Saudi Vision 2030 objectives. 🇸🇦
